snippet.title: 10 Things to NEVER Do as a Dementia Caregiver
snippet.description:
📞 Ready for concierge level support? Work with Dr. Sinclair by scheduling your call here: https://www.confidentcaregiveracademy.com/schedule
📥 New to Caregiving? Download the Free Care Starter Kit →https://www.confidentcaregiveracademy.com/confident-care-starter-kit-5steps-to-dementia-care

If you’re caring for someone with dementia, there are 10 things you should never do, not because you’re doing anything wrong, but because the dementia brain can’t process the world the same way anymore. These 10 common habits (that almost every caregiver unconsciously does) can make behaviors worse, increase arguing, and leave you feeling exhausted and defeated.

In this video, neuropsychologist and dementia care specialist Dr. Camille Sinclair walks you through the 10 things to avoid, why they backfire in the dementia brain, and exactly what to do instead.

You’ll learn the brain science behind arguing, repetition, refusal, and emotional outbursts, explained in a simple, compassionate way meant for real-life family caregivers.

Whether you’re new to dementia caregiving or years into the journey, these 10 shifts will help you:
Reduce arguing and defensiveness
Stop triggering confusion and overwhelm
Communicate more effectively
Calm tense situations
Build connection even when memory is fading
Understand what behaviors actually mean

You deserve to feel confident and supported, and this video gives you essential tools to create calmer, easier days with your loved one.

snippet.title: Why My Mom Lives in Memory Care | The Realities of Dementia Caregiving 💜
snippet.description:
Teachable Moment: 

I know you don't mean any harm when CONSTANTLY asking but some things are hurtful anyway. DO YOU KNOW HOW HARD IS IT TO WATCH A PARENT WITH DEMENTIA LIVE IN MEMORY CARE? I know I make it look easy but it's NOT. 

Here are some things you should know since the question is such a HOT TOPIC: 

💜 1. Dementia Is Unpredictable
One moment everything seems fine, the next it can turn into aggression, confusion, or unsafe behavior. Memory care provides structure, trained staff, and an environment designed to keep them safe​ in a LOCKED facility.

💜 2. Safety Comes First
Falls, wandering, aggression, and medical needs are real risks. At home, it’s often impossible to provide 24/7 supervision without sacrificing the caregiver’s health. Memory care facilities are designed to reduce those risks.

💜 3. Caregivers Deserve Peace Too

Family members cannot live in constant chaos. Everyone deserves peace. Memory care can restore balance and protect everyone’s mental, emotional, and physical well-being.

💜 4. Violence Is Real
Not all people with dementia become violent — but some do. From being scratched, bitten, or hit, caregivers may endure abuse no one should have to tolerate at home. Memory care ensures both the parent and family remain safe.

💜 5. Love ​vs. Care
Placing a loved one in memory care is not ​ALWAYS abandonment — it’s an act of love. It means recognizing when their needs surpass what one person (or even a family) can provide, and choosing the best environment for their dignity, health, and freedom.​ I can love my mom to the moon and back but I cannot provide her the 24/7 CARE she requires and deserves. 

💜 6. Trained Professionals Are Essential
Memory care staff are trained in dementia behaviors, de-escalation, and medical monitoring. Even the most devoted family caregiver can’t replace a whole team of trained professionals available 24/7.

💜 7. Everyone’s Journey Is Different
There is no “one-size-fits-all” dementia journey. What works for one family may not work for another. Respect that every family has the right to choose what keeps their loved one safest and happiest.​ Remember, IT ALSO DEPENDS ON THE TEMPERMENT OF THE PERSON REQUIRING THE CARE! 

👉🏽 If this message resonates with you, please LIKE this video, SUBSCRIBE to the channel, and tap the notification bell 🔔 so you don’t miss future caregiving updates.
💬 Share your thoughts in the comments — have you ever been judged for your caregiving choices? Let’s support each other through this journey.

#DementiaAwareness #MemoryCare #CaregiverLife #DivasAndDementia #DementiaJourney #CaregivingTruth #AlzheimersAwareness #ElderCare #FamilyCaregiver #CaregiverSupport

snippet.title: 13 Griefs Dementia Caregivers Carry… In Silence
snippet.description:
You can love the person you’re caring for—and still feel grief, resentment, and exhaustion. That doesn’t make you a bad caregiver. It makes you human.

In this video, I’m sharing 13 griefs dementia caregivers carry in silence...the hidden emotional weight most people never talk about. From the slow loss of your loved one to the sacrifice of your own dreams, these are the unspoken realities behind dementia care.

👉 If any of these hit home, leave a comment below. Your story can help another caregiver feel less alone.

🎥 Subscribe for more support, mindset shifts, and real talk about dementia caregiving.

 Sign up for our FREE Dementia Dose newsletter here: https://tinyurl.com/dementiadose-yt

#DementiaCaregiver #CaregiverGrief #UnspokenGrief #DementiaSupport #Careblazers

Hi, I’m Dr. Natali Edmonds, a board-certified geropsychologist specializing in dementia care. Careblazers started as an idea during a hiking trip—I wanted to create free, expert-led dementia education that caregivers could access from anywhere. Our mission? Make dementia caregiving easier. Whether your loved one has Alzheimer’s, frontotemporal, Lewy body, vascular, or mixed dementia, we believe that to create a dementia-friendly world, we must first create a caregiver-friendly world.

snippet.title: 10 Tips for Dementia Caregivers - Caring for Loved Ones with Memory Loss (and avoid burnout)
snippet.description:
Don't forget to like, share, and subscribe for more valuable content on dementia care and support!

For more information about Alzheimer’s disease, related dementia and aging, join AgeWiseU  at MelissaBPhD.com/join 

Are you:
❓A caregiver for a person living with dementia?
❓An adult child caring for an aging parent?
❓Someone who wants to learn more about aging well?

Are you struggling with:
😤The amount of time it takes to find answers on your own?
😤Finding conflicting information online?
😩Worried your loved one may not be safe at home alone anymore?
😩 Feeling anxious and overwhelmed about what might be down the road and how to navigate these changes?
😡 Having conflict with the person because they won’t listen to you or follow advice?

These issues are not easy. It’s a complicated journey, full of uncertainty, questions and struggles ~ but it doesn’t have to be.

Why you should join AgeWiseU:
✅ Expert advice and guidance from a nurse/ nurse practitioner with nearly 30 years of experience caring for older adults and their families
✅ Immediately actionable, practical tips prevent, manage, and live life well with Alzheimer’s disease 
✅ Join our community to get the latest news and information you need about Alzheimer’s disease and aging well

🎯 Learn more at MelissaBPhD.com/join
=============

“If you aren't taking care of yourself, you can't take care of anybody else.”
—Melissa Batchelor, PhD, RN, FNP, FGSA, FAAN

Caring for individuals living with dementia is a profound act of love and dedication, but it also comes with its unique set of challenges. Caregivers often find themselves facing a tough journey filled with uncertainty, frustration, and emotional strain. In this episode, we'll talk about ways to help caregivers, offering insights to reduce stress and prevent burnout.
Check out the 10 tips in this video to better take care of yourself!

Remember, caring for someone with dementia is both challenging and rewarding. By implementing these tips and accessing available resources, you can navigate this journey with resilience and compassion.

snippet.title: Caregiving for a parent with dementia is A LOT to adjust to #familycaregiver #seniors #dementia
snippet.description:
Last year my partner and I became part of the sandwich generation club. In the midst of raising a daughter, who was 10 at the time, we decided to move my partner, Gia's 83-year old mom in with us to become her caregivers.
Gia's mom Lola, has dementia.  So needless to say our lives changed drastically. 

On this channel I normally talk about food, Lola needs soft and lower sodium meals...but honestly an even bigger thing to get used to, was round the clock care that Lola requires....and having to be at home for her the majority of the time.

For reference, Lola is in the stage of dementia that I like to describe as the sweet toddler phase.  She somewhat knows what's going on, but needs a lot of guidance.  With out help, she's pretty easy to keep entertained throughout the day, but we always have to be home so she doesn't get into trouble
I know that a lot of people are caregiving for grandparents, aging parents, or loved ones of all different ages and it can be very isolating.  So I figured I would start to share little glimpses of our day to day lives.

How do you entertain a senior with dementia all day?

What does a caregivers life actually look like? 

How do you keep your sanity when you are stuck at home most of the time?

Linked is the full video video where I walk you through what a weekend in the life of a caregiver looks like.

Whether you are a caregiver yourself and curious about what other people are doing or are thinking about moving an elderly parent in with you to take care of them, I hope this will bring you a little bit of joy and insight.

snippet.title: If you’re a caregiver for someone with dementia, watch this
snippet.description:
New research shows a major gap in caregiving support: fewer than 3% of older adults with dementia or cognitive impairment have a family caregiver formally registered for shared access to their electronic health record portal, even though this access lets caregivers see records, message providers, and stay in the loop on care. Many families are sharing passwords instead of registering properly, which creates security risks and confusion for clinical staff. If you’re a caregiver, ask your loved one’s clinic how to set up proxy access today.

localized.title: If you’re a caregiver for someone with dementia, watch this
localized.description:
New research shows a major gap in caregiving support: fewer than 3% of older adults with dementia or cognitive impairment have a family caregiver formally registered for shared access to their electronic health record portal, even though this access lets caregivers see records, message providers, and stay in the loop on care. Many families are sharing passwords instead of registering properly, which creates security risks and confusion for clinical staff. If you’re a caregiver, ask your loved one’s clinic how to set up proxy access today.

• Southerland et al. Few Caregivers of Older Adults With Dementia Have Shared Access to Their Care Recipients’ Electronic Health Record Portal, Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 2026.

snippet.title: How to Care for Yourself as a dementia caregiver
snippet.description:
How do you care for yourself while caring for someone with dementia, especially when caregiver burnout is already setting in?

In this video, I explain what self-care for dementia caregivers actually looks like in real life. We talk about protecting your mental health, managing guilt, finding small moments of relief, and why caring for yourself is not selfish or optional when you’re supporting someone with dementia.
This video is for caregivers who feel exhausted, overwhelmed, or stretched too thin and want practical, compassionate guidance that fits real caregiving life.

I also share why having the right support matters—whether that’s leaning on family, professionals, or trusted resources like @aplaceformom574 which helps families understand care options and connect with support so caregivers don’t have to do everything alone.

Learn more or connect with an advisor here: https://www.aplaceformom.com/caregiver-resources?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Video&utm_campaign=InfluencerJanuary&utm_content=DementiaCareBlazersYouTube3HowtoCareForYourself&attribution_ID=108 

This video is sponsored by @aplaceformom574  a free no-cost senior living advisory service that helps families explore care options when caregiving becomes overwhelming. Whether you’re noticing early signs that additional support might be needed or you’re actively searching for the right memory care or assisted living setting, A Place for Mom can connect you with a dedicated advisor to help you understand your options and take the next step with confidence.

Support isn’t a sign you’re failing. Support is what helps you keep going.
You don’t have to do this alone.

snippet.title: When Is It Time To Move Your Loved One To Memory Care? | Teepa snow
snippet.description: Teepa Snow, MS, OTR/L, FAOTA is an Occupational Therapist with over 40 years of clinical and academic experience. Her life’s mission is to shed a positive light on dementia, which is why she founded the GEMS State Model for understanding the progression of dementia and the Positive Approach® training strategies. Her company, Positive Approach to Care (PAC) provides online and in-person education and products to support those living with brain change.

snippet.title: Caring for Mom With Dementia. 💔 #caregiverlife #dementiacaregiver #mom
snippet.description:
One of the most beautiful ways my mom and I connected during her dementia journey was through music. When words failed her, songs still reached her heart. We’d sing together, and for those moments, it was like the disease didn’t matter. Music calmed her anxiety, helped with transitions, and brought us both so much comfort. It was our way of communicating when everything else felt too hard. The power of music really is incredible, and I’m so grateful for those moments of peace we shared. 💜

snippet.title: How To Understand Dementia As A Caregiver!
snippet.description:
Understanding Dementia as a Caregiver 🧠

Adria Thompson with @belightcare  shares how important it is for caregivers to enter the world of individuals living with dementia. Recognizing that dementia is a real medical condition, like heart failure, helps shift our perspective. When we see challenging behaviors as responses to a brain issue rather than just being difficult, it fosters understanding and patience in caregiving.

snippet.title: How to cope with caregiver GUILT when caring for a parent
snippet.description:
Caregiver guilt is one of the most common and least talked-about parts of caring for a parent with dementia. If you're feeling like you're never doing enough, you're not alone. Understanding caregiver guilt is the first step to releasing it so you can show up for your loved one without burning out.

snippet.title: What Dementia Caregivers Wish More People Knew (Day 17)
snippet.description:
Caregivers are more than just caregivers. 💙
Many family caregivers are juggling work, relationships, and their own health while providing unpaid care for a loved one with dementia. It often feels like a full-time job, but without the pay or recognition.

If you know a caregiver, reach out—a little kindness can go a long way. 💬
